title: Output-only feedback cannot localise an agent's failure
problem: I can see that my agent's result is wrong, but nothing tells me which step made it wrong, so my feedback cannot be acted on.
symptom: The agent oscillates between failure modes across iterations instead of converging: each fix trades one visible defect for another.
why_now: Tracing tooling has converged on spans around tool calls and token usage, which records THAT a step ran, not the execution state it produced. The mapping from internal state to visible outcome is many-to-one, so output-level judgement cannot invert it.
existing: Trace/span tooling (OpenTelemetry-based agent tracing): captures call structure and cost, not intermediate correctness.
LLM-as-judge on final output: scores the same output layer where the information is already lost.
Manual transcript review: does not scale and still reads the output, not the state.

evidence.title: The Observability Gap: Why Output-Level Human Feedback Fails for LLM Coding Agents
evidence.quote: bugs originate in code logic and execution state, while human evaluation occurs only at the output layer, and the many-to-one mapping from internal states to visible outcomes prevents symptom-level feedback from reliably identifying root causes
evidence.note: Same paper measures 0% full-scene success under output-only feedback, and reports that injecting minimal code-level knowledge restored convergence - i.e. the bottleneck was feedback observability, not model competence. Accepted to CHI 2026 Workshop on Human-Agent Collaboration.

evidence.title: INC-0007: diagnose stalled work from the duration distribution, not the outcome
evidence.quote: A success predicate defined as 'the output file exists' hides a chronically over-budget step.
evidence.note: Independent corroboration from operations rather than a lab: an outcome-level success signal concealed a step that was failing structurally for many iterations.

build_hypothesis: A step-level state recorder that snapshots the agent's declared intermediate state and diffs consecutive attempts, so a reviewer can see WHICH state transition changed rather than only that the output changed.

check.manual_question: When a run produces a wrong final answer, can you identify WHICH step produced the wrong intermediate state, or only that the output is wrong? If you only have final-output signal, feedback cannot localise the bug.
check.rationale: Intermediate observability cannot be detected from source: a repo can emit rich traces and still record nothing about execution STATE. Asking is honest; guessing from the presence of a tracing import is not.
